rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening the breast means opening, widening, and softening the Prophet’s heart through faith, prophethood, knowledge, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: نفتح ونوسع ونلين لك قلبك بالإيمان والنبوة والعلم والحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden that weighed on the Prophet’s back was lifted and had weakened him; an exhausted camel worn down by travel is also called naqḍ.
rows.anchor: وحططنا عنك وزرك الذي أنقض ظهرك أثقل ظهرك فأوهنه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He explains the burden as breaking the Prophet’s back when he heard its naqiḍ, meaning its sound.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: كسر ظهرك حين سمع نقيضه

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: They identify the burden with what the Prophet had done before Islam.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة والضحاك: يعني ما سلف منه في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: He interprets the burden as error and inadvertence.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: يعني الخطأ والسهو

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The burden means the community’s sins, attributed to the Prophet because his heart was occupied and concerned with them.
rows.anchor: ذنوب أمتك فأضافها إليه لاشتغال قلبه بها واهتمامه لها

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They understand the burden as the duties of prophethood and its responsibilities, which God made lighter for him.
rows.anchor: يعني خففنا عليك أعباء النبوة والقيام بأمرها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God protected the Prophet from bearing sin.
rows.anchor: وعصمناك عن احتمال الوزر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Asked by the Prophet about raising his mention, Gabriel conveyed God’s saying that whenever God is mentioned, the Prophet is mentioned with Him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سأل جبرائيل عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says the Prophet’s mention is joined to God’s: when God is mentioned, Muhammad is mentioned with Him.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ورفعنا لك ذكرك، قال: إذا ذكرت ذكرت معي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: God raises Muhammad’s mention in this world and the next, since sermons, witness statements, and prayers all proclaim his messengership alongside God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: يرفع الله ذكره في الدنيا والآخرة، فليس خطيب ولا متشهد ولا صاحب صلاة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says the Prophet’s mention is raised through the call to prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني بالتأذين

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: His poem praises the prophetic seal from God as renowned, shining, and witnessed, illustrating the Prophet’s raised mention.
rows.anchor: يقول حسان بن ثابت يمدح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أغر عليه للنبوة خاتم … من الله مشهور

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: The continuation of Hassan’s poem says the Prophet’s name is joined to God’s name in the five daily calls to witness.
rows.anchor: وضم الإله اسم النبي الى اسمه … إذا قال في الخمس المؤذن أشهد

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: He interprets the raised mention as God making remembrance of Muhammad complete faith in Him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء: يعني جعلت تمام الإيمان بي بذكرك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view is that God raised the Prophet’s mention among the angels in heaven.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ورفعنا لك ذكرك عند الملائكة في السماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view connects the raised mention to God’s covenant with the prophets, requiring them to believe in Muhammad and acknowledge his merit.
rows.anchor: بأخذ ميثاقه على النبيين وإلزامهم الإيمان به والإقرار بفضله

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: He says the prophets’ aspirations circle the Throne while Muhammad’s is above it, explaining the uniquely exalted mention.
rows.anchor: همم الأنبياء تجول حول العرش وهمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فوق العرش

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: He adds that creatures will seek Muhammad’s intercession on Judgment Day because they know his standing with God.
rows.anchor: ومفزع الخلق يوم القيامة إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم كمفزعهم إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hardship is the Prophet’s struggle against polytheists and his difficult mission; its ease is relief and victory that brings them to accept the truth willingly or unwillingly.
rows.anchor: مع الشدة التي أنت فيها من جهاد المشركين، ومزاولة ما أنت بسبيله يسرا ورخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the promise confirms it and strengthens hope.
rows.anchor: كرره لتأكيد الوعد وتعظيم الرجاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation assigns the first ease to this world and the repeated ease to the hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فإن مع العسر يسرا: في الدنيا، إن مع العسر يسرا: في الآخرة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After the verse came down, the Prophet told his companions to rejoice: ease had arrived and one hardship would not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ابشروا فقد جاءكم اليسر لن يغلب عسر يسرين»

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He swears that even if hardship were hidden in a burrow, ease would seek it out; one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: والذي نفسي بيده، لو كان العسر في جحر لطلبه اليسر

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: They explain the two-eases saying from Arabic definiteness: repeated definite hardship denotes one, while repeated indefinite ease denotes two.
rows.anchor: لأنه عرف العسر ونكر اليسر، ومن عادة العرب إذا ذكرت اسما معرفة ثم أعادته فهو هو

rows.speaker: الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني
rows.claim: He rejects the grammar offered for one hardship and two eases: repeating a definite noun and an indefinite noun does not force one sword but two in the example sentence.
rows.anchor: لا يجب على هذا التدريج إذا قال الرجل: إن مع الفارس سيفا إن مع الفارس سيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying means one hardship cannot overcome both promised eases; it can overcome worldly ease, but the hereafter’s lasting ease cannot be defeated.
rows.anchor: إنما يغلب أحدهما وهو يسر الدنيا، فأما يسر الآخرة فدائم غير زايل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was poor and mocked by the polytheists, who offered to gather wealth for him; he grieved, thinking they rejected him because of poverty.
rows.anchor: بعث نبيه (عليه السلام) مقلا مخففا فعيره المشركون لفقره، حتى قالوا أنجمع لك مالا؟ فاغتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verses recount God’s favors, while the prefixed fa in the first ease clause links it as a promise of immediate worldly relief and wealth.
rows.anchor: فهذا ذكر امتنانه عليه، ثم ابتدأ ما وعده من الغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed fa in fa-inna signals coordination or response; it reassures the Prophet not to grieve over their words, promising ease soon in this world.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه دخول الفاء في قوله (فإن) ولا يدخل الفاء أبدا إلا في عطف أو جواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly promise came true when God opened the Arab towns to the Prophet and expanded his means until he could give two hundred camels.
rows.anchor: ووسع ذات يده، حتى يهب المائتين من الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause begins a separate favor for the hereafter; lacking a conjunction, it generalizes to believers, whose worldly hardship is surely followed by ease in the next life.
rows.anchor: ومجازه: إن مع العسر في الدنيا للمؤمنين يسرا في الآخرة لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith means the single worldly hardship cannot overcome both the worldly ease promised to the Prophet and the enduring ease promised to believers in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: لن يغلب عسر الدنيا اليسر الذي وعد الله المؤمنين في الدنيا، واليسر الذي وعدهم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares this wording to the two feast months not both being diminished: two things are not jointly overcome by one event.
rows.anchor: كقوله (عليه السلام) «شهرا عيد لا ينقصان» أي لا يجتمعان في النقصان

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: He says that with hardship in this world comes the reward of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: مع [أختها] بالدنيا جزاء الجنة

rows.speaker: القاسم
rows.claim: He describes the gladness of this happiness as extending from the dawn hours of worldly life to the pleasure of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال القاسم: [بردا هذه السعادة من أسحار] الدنيا إلى رضوان العقبى

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The common reading pronounces the sīn lightly in both repetitions of yusr.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة بتخفيف السينين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وعيسى
rows.claim: They read both instances with a damma on the sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعيسى، بضمهما

rows.speaker: قراءة عبد الله
rows.claim: The codex attributed to Abdullah has the ease clause only once, without repetition.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله: إن مع العسر يسرا، مرة واحدة غير مكررة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Ibn Abbas to rely on God, seek Him in ease and hardship, remain patient, and know that patience brings victory, distress brings relief, and hardship comes with ease.
rows.anchor: فقال لي: «يا غلام» ، قلت: لبيك يا رسول الله، قال: «احفظ الله يحفظك

rows.speaker: العتبي
rows.claim: Al-Utbi says an unseen caller answered his grief with a poem urging him to recall the opening of al-Sharh, because hardship is between two eases; God then removed his distress.
rows.anchor: سمعت العتبي يقول: كنت ذات يوم في البادية بحالة من الغم

rows.speaker: إسحاق بن بهلول
rows.claim: His poem counsels against despair during a difficult day by remembering that easier times have come during a long life.
rows.anchor: فلا تيأس وإن أعسرت يوما … فقد أيسرت في دهر طويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fansab derives from exertion and means laboring diligently; another interpretation tells him to sit for tashahhud after prayer, then stand to supplicate.
rows.anchor: وقوله فانصب من النصب، وهو التعب والدأب في العمل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: When finished conveying the message, the Prophet should seek forgiveness for himself and the believers.
rows.anchor: عن حيان، عن الكلبي: إذا فرغت من تبليغ الرسالة

rows.speaker: جنيد
rows.claim: When finished with people’s affairs, he should strive in worship of God.
rows.anchor: عن جنيد: فإذا فرغت من أمر الخلق، فاجتهد في عبادة الحق

rows.speaker: أبو العباس بن عطاء
rows.claim: After conveying revelation, he should exert himself in seeking intercession.
rows.anchor: عن أبو العباس بن عطاء: فإذا فرغت من تبليغ الوحي، فانصب في طلب الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should direct his desire to his Lord in every circumstance and toward no one else.
rows.anchor: وإلى ربك فارغب في جميع أحوالك [لا] إلى سواه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: When free of worldly occupations, one should empty the heart for concerns of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إذا فرغت من أشغال الدنيا، ففرغ قلبك لهموم العقبى

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Remember the Lord when free of everything besides Him.
rows.anchor: عن جعفر: اذكر ربك على فراغ منك عن كل ما دونه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: After worship, exert yourself in turning away from it for fear it may be rejected; desire God and seek forgiveness for your deed in shame.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إذا فرغت من العبادة، فانصب إلى الإعراض عنها مخافة ردها عليك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A recitation practice transmitted through Ubayy is to pronounce takbir at the end of each surah beginning with al-Duha; the Prophet instructed Ubayy to do so.
rows.anchor: أخبره أبي بن كعب أنه قرأ على النبي (صلى الله عليه وآله) ، فأمره بذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وعكرمة وإبراهيم وعطاء بن أبي رباح وجابر بن زيد ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They identify the fig and olive as the familiar fruits people eat and press for oil.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وعكرمة وإبراهيم وعطاء بن أبي رباح

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After eating a gift of figs, the Prophet said that if any fruit had descended from Paradise it would be this; he said it has no pits and benefits hemorrhoids and gout.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: أهدي للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طبق من تين فأكل منه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet praised olive wood as a good siwak, said it sweetens the mouth, and called it his and earlier prophets’ tooth-stick from the blessed tree.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم [يقول] نعم السواك الزيتون من الشجرة المباركة

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار وقتادة وابن زيد وعبد الرحمن بن غنيم
rows.claim: They interpret the fig as Damascus Mosque and the olive as Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار وقتادة وابن زيد وعبد الرحمن بن غنيم: التين: مسجد دمشق

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says the fig and olive signify two mosques in Syria.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك: هما مسجدان بالشام

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: He identifies the fig as the Companions of the Cave’s mosque and the olive as the mosque of Ilya, taking the names to mean their growing places.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب: التين: مسجد أصحاب الكهف، والزيتون: مسجد إيليا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He says the fig and olive are two mountains.
rows.anchor: أبو مكين، عن عكرمة: جبلان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through Atiyya, he identifies the fig with Noah’s mosque built on al-Judi and the olive with Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: عن عطية، عن ابن عباس: التين: مسجد نوح الذي [بناه] على الجودي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Through Nahshal, he identifies the fig as the Sacred Mosque and the olive as al-Aqsa.
rows.anchor: عن نهشل، عن الضحاك: التين: المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: رجل من أهل الشام
rows.claim: A Syrian commentator told al-Farra that the fig mountains run from Helwan to Hamadan and the olive mountains are in Syria.
rows.anchor: سمعت الفراء يقول: سمعت رجلا من أهل الشام وكان صاحب تفسير قال: التين: جبال ما بين حلوان إلى همدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mount Sinai means the mountain of Moses.
rows.anchor: وطور سينين يعني جبل موسى

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He says Sinin means bridge in the Ethiopian language.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: السينين: الجسر بلغة الحبش

rows.speaker: الحكم والنضر
rows.claim: They say any mountain where plants grow can be called Mount Sinin, just as vegetation grows both on plain land and in mountains.
rows.anchor: الحكم والنضر عنه: كل جبل ينبت فهو طور سينين، كما ينبت في السهل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says tur means mountain and sinin means blessed.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد: الطور الجبل، وسينين: المبارك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets Sinin as blessed and good.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة: المبارك الحسن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: A mountain with fruit-bearing trees is called Sinin or Sina in the Nabatean language.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل: كل جبل فيه شجرة مثمرة فهو سينين وسينا وهو بلغة النبط

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He explains the phrase as a wooded mountain.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي: يعني الجبل المشجر

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: He identifies the fig as Kufa, the olive as Syria, and Mount Sinin as a mountain bearing many kinds of trees.
rows.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب: التين: الكوفة، والزيتون: الشام، وطور سينين: جبل فيه ألوان الأشجار

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: He lists four sacred mountains: Damascus, Jerusalem, Moses’ mountain, and Mecca, respectively called Tur Tinna, Tur Zayta, Tur Sina, and Tur Yatmana.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: أربعة أجبال مقدسة بين يدي الله سبحانه، طور تينا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: He recited the verse at Mecca with the reading ‘Tur Sina’; the narrator thought he did so to teach the city’s sanctity.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن عمرو قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقرأ بمكة في المغرب: والتين والزيتون وطور سيناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca, described as safe.
rows.anchor: وهذا البلد الأمين الآمن، يعني مكة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: His cited verse demonstrates that amin here means protected or safe.
rows.anchor: وأنشد الفراء: ألم تعلمي يا أسم ويحك أنني … حلفت يمينا لا أخون أميني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans were created upright and in the best image, unlike other creatures made bent forward on their faces.
rows.anchor: أعدل قامة وأحسن صورة، وذلك أنه خلق كل شيء منكبا على وجهه إلا الإنسان

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن ظاهر
rows.claim: He describes human excellence as intellect, instruction by divine command, discernment, tall stature, and the ability to take food by hand.
rows.anchor: مزينا بالعقل، مؤدبا بالأمر، مهذبا بالتمييز، مديد القامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lowering means return to decrepit old age, when life declines, the body weakens, and the mind departs.
rows.anchor: يعني إلى أرذل العمر، ينقص عمره ويضعف بدنه ويذهب عقله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Some people reached extreme old age in the Prophet’s time, and God revealed an excuse for them and promised the reward of their earlier deeds.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: [إن] نفرا ردوا إلى أرذل العمر على عهد رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation identifies the olive as the Mosque of al-Aqsa.
rows.anchor: والزيتون: المسجد الأقصى

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Extreme age does not harm an old person if God ends his life in the best state of deeds.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: لم يضر هذا الشيخ الهرم كبره إذا ختم الله تعالى له بأحسن ما كان يعمل

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: They say the lowly include the weak, elderly, and chronically ill; the indefinite phrase generalizes the whole class, unlike a definite form referring to known people.
rows.anchor: السافلون: الضعفى والهرمى والزمنى، فقوله (أسفل سافلين) نكرة تعم الجنس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Anas says children’s good deeds benefit parents before puberty and sins are unrecorded; later, at extreme senility, the same good deeds as in health are recorded and sins omitted.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «المولود حتى يبلغ الحنث ما عمل من حسنة كتبت لوالديه

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: They interpret the return to the lowest state as a return to Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة: يعني ثم رددناه الى النار

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: He says the person is returned to the fire in the worst form, as a pig.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: يعني إلى النار في شر صورة، في صورة خنزير

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: He says Hell’s gates are arranged below one another and filled from the lowest, explaining the lowest of the low.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال: أبواب جهنم بعضها أسفل من بعض، فيبدأ بالأسفل فيملأ

rows.speaker: مصحف عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah’s codex reads the phrase with the definite article: ‘the lowest of the low.’
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله، (أسفل السافلين) بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers whose minds and deeds cease in old age still receive the same record of good works they performed when young, healthy, and strong.
rows.anchor: فأنه يكتب لهم في حال هرمهم وخرفهم مثل الذي كانوا يعملونه في حال شبابهم وصحتهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He explains their reward as given without their having to perform the deeds then.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: أجر بغير عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following challenge to the denier is a compelling argument and a rebuke to the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: إلزاما للحجة وتوبيخا للكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another version identifies the horse in the preceding account as belonging to Mirthad ibn Abi Mirthad al-Ghanawi.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى وفرس لمرثد بن أبي مرثد الغنوي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He first says the chargers are horses raiding in God’s cause, then returning at night to prepare food and kindle a fire.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس حدثه قال: بينما أنا في الحجر جالس أتاني رجل فسأل عن العاديات ضبحا، فقال له: الخيل

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali rejects the horse interpretation because at Badr, Islam’s first expedition, the Muslims had only two horses; he says the chargers are camels from Arafat to Muzdalifa and Mina.
rows.anchor: والله إن كانت لأول غزوة في الإسلام بدر، وما كان معنا إلا فرسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After hearing Ali’s argument, Ibn Abbas withdrew his interpretation and adopted Ali’s view; Ibn Masud, Muhammad ibn Umayr, Muhammad ibn Kab, and al-Suddi also held it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فنزعت عن قولي ورجعت إلى الذي قال علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says a camel reading takes dabḥa as stretched necks during travel, treating ḍabaḥa and ḍabaʿa as synonyms and citing Safiyya’s poem.
rows.anchor: وضبحت وضبعت بمعنى واحد، قالت صفية بنت عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: عكرمة وعطاء والضحاك
rows.claim: They say the horses strike sparks with their hooves as they travel over stones and gravel.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة وعطاء والضحاك: هي الخيل توري النار بحوافرها

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They say Arabs call such a fire the fire of Abu Habbab; he was a notoriously stingy pre-Islamic man who extinguished his cooking fire whenever anyone might benefit from it.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: والعرب تسمي تلك النار نار أبي حباحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means ‘those that strike sparks,’ shifting from the verbal noun to a derived participial form.
rows.anchor: ومجاز الآية: والقادحات قدحا فخالف بين الصدر والمصدر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He understands the image as horses stirring up war and hostility among their riders.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: هي الخيل تهيج للحرب ونار العداوة بين أصحابها وفرسانها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report from Ibn Abbas, horses raid for God and return at night to prepare food and kindle their fire.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: هي الخيل تغير في سبيل الله ثم تأوي إلى الليل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: They interpret it as a man’s plotting; Arabic speakers say they will ‘strike sparks’ for someone when plotting against him.
rows.anchor: مجاهد وزيد بن أسلم: هي مكر الرجل والعرب تقول إذا أراد الرجل أن يمكر لصاحبه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He says the sparks refer to men of war.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: يعني رجال الحرب

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He says men’s tongues kindle fires through the force of their speech.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: هي ألسنة الرجال توري النار من عظيم ما تتكلم به

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: A view transmitted by Ibn Jurayj compares successful deeds to a peg succeeding when it catches a spark.
rows.anchor: ابن جريج عن بعضهم: فالمنجحات عملا كنجاح الوتد إذا أوري

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: He identifies the sparks as fires kindled at Jamʿ.
rows.anchor: محمد بن كعب: هي النيران بجمع

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the dawn raiders as horses carrying their riders against the enemy at daybreak.
rows.anchor: يعني الخيل، تغير بفرسانها على العدو وقت الصبح، هذا قول أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: He says they are camels rushing with their riders from Jamʿ to Mina on the Day of Sacrifice; the rite delays departure until morning, and ghāra means to travel quickly.
rows.anchor: قال القرظي: هي الإبل تدفع بركبانها يوم النحر من جمع إلى منى

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: He reads fa-aththarna with a doubled consonant, meaning the beasts leave an impact at the place they reach, omitted from the wording because it is understood.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة فأثرن بالتشديد من التأثير به أي بذلك المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqʿ means dust; wasatna bihi means entering the middle of a group, and the light, doubled, and derived forms all mean to enter the midst.
rows.anchor: نقعا أي غبارا فوسطن به أي دخلن به وسطهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He reads wasatna with a doubled sīn, meaning the animals gather the enemy into a mass or battalion.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة فوسطن، بالتشديد جمعا أي جمع العدو وهم الكتيبة

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: He interprets the gathered assembly as the pilgrims’ gathering at Mina.
rows.anchor: وقال القرظي: يعني جمع منى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The striking event scatters people like moths, understood here as birds falling into fire; scattered means dispersed.
rows.anchor: وهي الطير التي تتساقط في النار، المبثوث: المتفرق

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He compares the terrified, swarming people to locusts piling upon one another.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: الغوغاء: الجراد يركب بعضه بعضا من الهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains become like carded wool dyed in colors and loosened.
rows.anchor: كالصوف المصبوغ المبلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose scales weigh heavily have a pleasing, well-pleased-with-it life in Paradise.
rows.anchor: فهو في عيشة راضية مرضية في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the one whose scales are light, his destination and home are Hell.
rows.anchor: فأمه هاوية مسكنه ومأواه النار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says hāwat ummuh is a familiar Arabic expression used when someone falls into a severe predicament.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هي كلمة عربية، كان الرجل إذا وقع في أمر شديد قال: هوت أمه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret ‘his mother’ as his head, meaning the people fall headfirst into Hell; Qatada and Abu Salih adopted this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أراد أم رأسه، يعني أنهم يهوون في النار على رؤوسهم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: He reports an angel weighing each person’s deeds; a heavy scale brings a public proclamation of lasting felicity, while a light one brings lasting misery.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: إن ملكا من ملائكة الله عز وجل موكل يوم القيامة بميزان ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rivalry in boasting about wealth and numbers distracts people from obeying God and escaping His anger.
rows.anchor: شغلتكم المباهاة والمفاخرة بكثرة المال والعدد عن طاعة ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visiting the graves means dying and being buried in them.
rows.anchor: أي متم فدفنتم فيها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says the surah came down about Jews comparing which clan was larger, a contest that distracted them until they died astray.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت في اليهود قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان

rows.speaker: ابن بريدة
rows.claim: He says it came down about a clan among the Ansar who boasted against one another.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن بريدة: نزلت في فخذ من الأنصار تفاخروا

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They say two Quraysh clans disputed which had more leaders and numbers, then counted their dead in graves; Banu Sahm outnumbered Banu Abd Manaf by three households, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في حيين من قريش: بني عبد مناف وبني قصي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says a person’s real possessions are only what he eats and consumes, wears and wears out, or gives in charity and sends ahead.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه قال: انتهيت إلى رسول الله (عليه السلام) وهو يقرأ هذه الآية: ألهاكم التكاثر قال: يقول ابن آدم: ما لي ما لي،

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: He says Muslims remained unsure about punishment in the grave until ‘you will know’ was revealed, referring to the grave.
rows.anchor: وروى زر بن حبيش عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: ما زلنا نشك في عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first threat warns them, and its repetition reinforces the warning.
rows.anchor: كلا سوف تعلمون وعيد لهم ثم كلا سوف تعلمون والتكرير على التأكيد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He takes the first ‘you will know’ as addressing unbelievers and the second as addressing believers; his reading uses tāʾ first and yāʾ second.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كلا سوف تعلمون يعني الكفار ثم كلا سوف يعلمون يعني المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means certain knowledge, using an annexation of knowledge to certainty, as in the Qur’anic phrase ‘true certainty.’
rows.anchor: أي علما يقينا فأضاف العلم إلى اليقين لقوله سبحانه: إن هذا لهو حق اليقين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says certain knowledge is knowing that God will raise people after death.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كنا نحدث أن علم اليقين أن يعلم أن الله باعثه بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeing clause can function as a past-tense response to ‘if’: if they knew with certainty, they would see Hell in their hearts and then see it with their eyes.
rows.anchor: يصلح أن يكون في معنى المضي جوابا ل (لو) ، تقديره: لو تعلمون العلم اليقين لرأيتم الجحيم بقلوبكم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He takes certain knowledge to deter people from rivalry, then treats ‘you will see Hell’ as a fresh oath statement.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب مقاتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says certainty that they will see the Fire would distract them from their present pursuits.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه: لو علمتم يقينا أنكم ترون النار لشغلكم ذلك عما أنتم فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Three repetitions of kalla mark knowledge at death, in the grave, and at resurrection; the third is certain knowledge because what was hidden has become visible.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ذكر (كلا) ثلاث مرات أراد: تعلمون عند النزوع، وتعلمون في القبر، وتعلمون في القيامة

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The common reading uses a damma on the tāʾ in both occurrences of ‘you will surely see.’
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة لترون بضم التاء في الحرفين

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai reads with a damma in the first occurrence and fatḥa in the second; he transmits that reading from Ali.
rows.anchor: وضم الكسائي التاء في الأولى منهما وفتح الأخرى، ورواه عن علي

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali’s reading uses a damma on the first tāʾ and fatḥa on the second.
rows.anchor: عن علي أنه قرأ لترون الجحيم ثم لترونها بضم التاء الأولى وفتح الثانية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He prefers the first reading because the passage is emphatic and should not vary its wording.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: الأول أشبه بكلام العرب لأنه تغليظ فلا ينبغي أن يختلف لفظه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In another report through Ali al-Rida’s forebears, the Prophet identifies the blessing as fresh dates and cold water.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله (عليه السلام) في قول سبحانه: ثم لتسئلن يومئذ عن النعيم قال: «الرطب والماء البارد»

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: He says the blessing is cold water in summer and cites a report that God first asks whether He gave health and cold water.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر: هو الماء البارد في الصيف

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After a meal at al-Miqdad’s, the Prophet praised the cold water and advised drinking it as cold as possible because it helps the stomach and illness and prompts gratitude.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: «إذا شرب أحدكم الماء فليشرب أبرد ما يقدر عليه»

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: He says cool, fresh water draws praise from the heart.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا حاتم يقول: الماء البارد العذب يستخرج الحمد من جوف القلب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says the neighbor who refuses sweets for fear of failing to thank God is ignorant: cold water is a greater blessing than all sweets.
rows.anchor: فقال: ما أجهل جاركم بنعمة الله عليه بالماء البارد أكثر من نعمة بجميع الحلاوي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet names wheat bread, chilled water, and shade as blessings for which people will be asked.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن النبي (عليه السلام) في قول الله جل ثناؤه ثم لتسئلن يومئذ عن النعيم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar visit Abu al-Haytham, share dates, water, shade, and a meal, and the Prophet says this is among the blessings people will be asked about.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «هذا من النعيم الذي تسألون عنه»

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When companions asked how they could be questioned about blessing with only dates, water, and swords, the Prophet replied that this questioning would indeed occur.
rows.anchor: قال: «إن ذاك لكائن»

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says some of the Prophet’s community will bind butter and honey with refined flour and eat it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي قلابة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الله سبحانه: ثم لتسئلن يومئذ عن النعيم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: He says he would not enter a bathhouse because it is a newly introduced luxury; Mansur likewise avoided it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: لا يدخل الحمام فإنه مما أحدثوا من النعيم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: God will enumerate blessings on Judgment Day, including arranging the marriage a woman had requested for the servant.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله عن النبي (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) قال: «إن الله سبحانه ليعدد نعمه على العبد

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: In a report from Ikrima, God answers the companions’ question about their limited worldly comforts by pointing to shoes and cold water as blessings.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله سبحانه إلى نبيه: قل لهم: «أليس تحتذون النعال، وتشربون الماء البارد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells a needy man that shoes, shade, and cold water are blessings for which one is responsible.
rows.anchor: قال: «نعم، النعلان، والظل، والماء البارد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says the questioned blessing includes every pleasure of worldly life.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد لتسئلن يومئذ عن النعيم قال: عن كل لذة من لذات الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that beyond a dwelling, a covering cloth, and a morsel of food to strengthen the body, everything is blessing.
rows.anchor: قال: «بيت يقلك، وخرقة تواري عورتك، وكسرة تشد بها صلبك ما سوى ذلك نعيم»

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s report, takathur is wrongful accumulation and withholding; the passage follows people through graves and judgment, then names five blessings: full stomach, cold drink, sleep, shade, and sound constitution.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألهاكم التكاثر

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: He says one who names God before eating and praises Him afterward will not be asked about the blessing of that meal.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: من أكل فسمى الله وفرغ فحمد الله لم يسئل عن نعيم ذلك الطعام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies blessings as bodily health, hearing, and sight, which God will ask people how they used, citing the statement that hearing, sight, and heart will be questioned.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: النعيم صحة الأبدان والأسماع والأبصار

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: He interprets the blessing as well-being.
rows.anchor: أبو جعفر: العافية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet names a morsel that gives strength, water that quenches thirst, and a garment that covers as blessings asked about on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «النعيم المسؤول عنه يوم القيامة: كسرة تقويه، وماء يرويه، وثوب يواريه»

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: When offered honey, he said it was among the blessings people are asked about.
rows.anchor: أتي سعيد بن جبير بشربة عسل فقال: أما إن هذا من النعيم الذي يسئل عنه

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: He says the blessing is God’s gift of Muhammad and cites the verse that people recognize God’s favor and then deny it.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: يعني عما أنعم عليكم بمحمد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He identifies the blessing as health and free time.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: عن الصحة والفراغ

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He says the blessings are health, free time, and wealth, citing the Prophet’s saying that many people are cheated regarding health and free time.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: عن الصحة والفراغ والمال

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: He says even a deaf, blind, disabled, leprous person retains blessings in eating and drinking to satisfaction and being able to relieve himself easily.
rows.anchor: قال عروة بن محمد: كنا مع وهب بن منبه فرأينا رجلا أصم أعمى مقعدا

rows.speaker: عبد الله المزني
rows.claim: He marvels that enjoying food and then relieving oneself with ease is itself a blessing.
rows.anchor: قال بكر عن عبد الله المزني: يا لها من نعمة يأكل لذة ويخرج سرجا

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: He interprets the blessings as Islam and protection or concealment.
rows.anchor: أبو العالية: عن الإسلام والستر

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: He says the blessings include lighter religious duties and an accessible Quran.
rows.anchor: الحسين بن الفضل: تخفيف الشرائع وتيسير القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: He understands the blessings as all divine favors and benefits.
rows.anchor: أبو بكر الوراق: عن الآلاء والنعماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says al-asr means time or the age.
rows.anchor: والعصر قال ابن عباس: والدهر

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: He says al-asr means night and day, also called the two asrs, or morning and evening, likewise called the two asrs; Humayd ibn Thawr’s poem witnesses the paired expression.
rows.anchor: ابن كيسان: الليل والنهار ويقال لهما: العصران وللغداة والعشي أيضا: عصران

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says al-asr is the time from noon until sunset.
rows.anchor: الحسن: بعد زوال الشمس إلى غروبها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets it as the final hour of the day.
rows.anchor: قتادة: آخر ساعة من ساعات النهار

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He identifies al-asr as the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: صلاة العصر وهي الوسطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people are in loss except those who believe and do righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: فإنهم ليسوا في خسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawāsaw means urging and advising one another.
rows.anchor: وتواصوا وتحاثوا وأوصى بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They identify the truth that believers urge one another to uphold as the Quran.
rows.anchor: بالحق بالقرآن عن الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He says the truth means faith and affirmation of God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: بالإيمان والتوحيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is mutual exhortation to act according to the truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على العمل بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience means steadfastness in carrying out religious duties and upholding God’s command.
rows.anchor: على أداء الفرائض وإقامة أمر الله

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: He says human life declines with age into weakness, except believers, whose good works from youth, strength, and health continue to be recorded.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: أراد أن الإنسان إذا عمر في الدنيا وهرم لفي نقص وضعف

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: One reading attributed to Ali adds that a person remains in loss until the end of time.
rows.anchor: قال: [كان علي رضي الله عنه يقرأ ذلك] : إن الإنسان لفي خسر وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The same reading is attributed to Ibn Masud, extending the state of loss to the end of time.
rows.anchor: وكذلك هي في قراءة ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Another reading attributed to Ali renders al-asr as the vicissitudes of time and adds that the person remains in loss until time’s end.
rows.anchor: وكان علي يقرأها: والعصر، ونوائب الدهر، إن الإنسان لفي خسر، وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound reading is the one followed by the general reciters and standard codices.
rows.anchor: والقراءة الصحيحة ما عليه العامة والمصاحف

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy says he recited the surah to the Prophet and asked him for its interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة عن أبي بن كعب قال: قرأت على رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) والعصر فقلت:

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says al-asr is an oath by God on behalf of the audience at the day’s end; he identifies the person in loss with Abu Jahl and the believers, righteous deeds, truth, and patience in turn with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali.
rows.anchor: فقال: «والعصر قسم من الله أقسم لكم بآخر النهار» إن الإنسان لفي خسر قال: «أبو جهل بن هشام»

rows.speaker: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: While preaching from the Prophet’s pulpit, he recited the surah and repeated the same identifications of Abu Jahl, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali with its phrases.
rows.anchor: فوافيت علي بن عبد الله بن عباس يخطب على منبر رسول الله

rows.speaker: عطاء بن دينار
rows.claim: He notes that the wording condemns those heedless of prayer, not those merely heedless during prayer.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي قال: الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون ولم يقل في صلاتهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says the person prays for show and feels no regret when missing the prayer.
rows.anchor: هو الذي إن صلاها صلاها رياء وأن فاتته لم يندم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: He says they fail to pray at the proper times and do not complete bowing and prostration.
rows.anchor: لا يصلونها لمواقيتها ولا يتمون ركوعها ولا سجودها

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: He also says they turn their heads back and forth while prostrating.
rows.anchor: إذا سجد قال برأسه هكذا وهكذا ملتفتا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says they abandon prayer.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: هم الذين يتركون الصلاة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: He identifies al-maʿun as obligatory alms; Ibn Umar, al-Hasan, Qatada, Ibn al-Hanafiya, and al-Dahhak share this interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه ويمنعون الماعون قال: هي الزكاة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: He says al-maʿun means everyday tools such as an axe, bucket, cooking pot, and similar useful items.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله في الماعون قال: الفاس والدلو والقدر وأشباه ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Saeed ibn Jubayr interprets al-maʿun as borrowed goods and household utensils.
rows.anchor: وهي رواية سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس، مجاهد عنه: هو العارية ومتاع البيت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through Atiyya, Ibn Abbas is also said to interpret al-maʿun as obedience.
rows.anchor: عطية عنه: هو الطاعة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب والكلبي
rows.claim: They say al-maʿun is all customary kindness and help people exchange with one another.
rows.anchor: محمد بن كعب والكلبي: الماعون المعروف كله الذي يتعاطاه الناس فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والزهري ومقاتل
rows.claim: They say al-maʿun means wealth in Quraysh’s dialect; al-Aʿsha’s poem supports this lexical meaning.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن المسيب والزهري ومقاتل: الماعون: المال بلغة قريش، قال الأعشى

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He cites an Arab expression in which al-maʿun means obedience and compliance, illustrated by an unknown poet’s verse.
rows.anchor: تعطيك الماعون، أي الطاعة والانقياد، قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He also reports that some Arabs use maʿun for flowing water.
rows.anchor: وحكى الفراء أيضا عن بعضهم أنه قال: ماعون من الماء المعين

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: He derives the word from scarcity: maʿun names alms, charity, and kindness because they are a small part of much wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب: أصل الماعون من القلة، يقول العرب: ماله سعنة ولا معنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says al-maʿun means things that must not be withheld, such as water, salt, and fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الماعون ما لا يحل منعه مثل الماء والملح والنار

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report from Aisha, the Prophet says water, salt, and fire should not be withheld; sharing fire or salt earns the equivalent of what is cooked or seasoned, and giving water is likened to freeing sixty people or saving a life.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت: يا رسول الله ما الذي لا يحل منعه قال: «الماء والملح والنار»

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: His poem describes a people who do not withhold their help or the confession of God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: قال الراعي: قوم على الإسلام لما يمنعوا … ماعونهم ويمنعوا التهليلا
